introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1, JUNE 2023, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 4, 7, 9, 14, 20, 29, 40. 4 : bacteria, fungi et yeast peuvent tous provoquer une fermentation (cle visee d). 7 : cocktail party et buffet party utilisent peu de couverts (cle visee a). 9 : la reponse batter n'est pas dans les options. 14 : controlled by (signal electrique) ou powered by (energie chimique) (cle visee a). 20 et 29 : aucune cle etablie. 40 : chaque option contient une epice ou un condiment (cle visee d).

questions.enonce_markdown: An incorrect or unbalanced intake of nutrients cause:.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Malnutrition means "bad nutrition": the body receives too little, too much or the wrong proportions of nutrients, so the intake is incorrect or unbalanced. Under nutrition (too little) and over nutrition (too much) are only two forms of malnutrition, and underweight is one of the effects, not the name of the condition.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Fat from pork is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lard is the fat rendered from pork. Dripping is the fat that runs from roasted meat (usually beef), suet is the hard fat around the kidneys of beef or mutton, and butter is made from milk.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Absorption takes place mainly in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Digested food is absorbed mainly in the small intestine (especially the ileum), whose wall has a very large surface area. The villi are the tiny finger-like projections that do the absorbing, but they are a part of the small intestine, so the place named is the small intestine. The stomach absorbs very little (some water and alcohol) and the large intestine absorbs mostly water.

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown:
Fermentation is caused by:,

*Options as printed:* A) Bacteria   B) Parasites   C) Fungi   D) Yeast
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the kitchen, fermentation (for example the rising of bread dough or the making of palm wine) is most often caused by yeast, which feeds on sugar and produces carbon dioxide and alcohol. Yeast is itself a fungus and some bacteria also ferment foods (yoghurt, fermented cassava), so more than one option can be defended. The most specific and usual answer is yeast.

**Intended answer: D (Yeast).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The transparent protective coating in an egg is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cuticle (bloom) is the thin, transparent layer on the outside of the shell. It seals the pores and protects the egg against bacteria and loss of moisture. The chalazae are twisted cords that hold the yolk in the centre, the membranes lie inside the shell, and the thick white is part of the albumen.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Baking powder is categorized as a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Baking powder is a mixture of an alkali (sodium bicarbonate) and an acid. When it becomes wet and is heated it releases carbon dioxide, which makes the mixture rise. A gas produced by a chemical reaction means it is a chemical raising agent. Whisking and sieving are mechanical methods and yeast is a biological raising agent.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A food service where little or no cutlery is used is called:

*Options as printed:* A) Cocktail party   B) Buffet party   C) Luncheon party   D) Dinner party
questions.corrige_markdown:
At a cocktail party guests stand and eat small "finger foods" (canapes, savouries, small cakes) with the fingers, so little or no cutlery is needed. At a buffet party guests help themselves but usually still use a fork or spoon, and luncheon and dinner parties are seated meals with a full cover of cutlery. A buffet can also use little cutlery, so the printed question is open to discussion; cocktail party is the best fit.

**Intended answer: A (Cocktail party).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a stone fruit from below:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A stone fruit has a fleshy part around one hard stone that holds the seed. The apricot (like the plum, peach, mango and cherry) is the standard example. Water melon and grape have many small seeds. Dates also have one stone, but they are normally classed as dried or tree fruits, and the apricot is the clear classroom answer.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The mixture of flour ,liquid and egg is called:

*Options as printed:* A) Butter   B) Dough   C) Pastry   D) Paste
questions.corrige_markdown:
A mixture of flour, liquid (milk or water) and egg that is thin enough to pour or drop from a spoon is called a **batter** (used for pancakes, Yorkshire pudding and fritters). Batter is not among the four printed options. Dough is a stiff mixture of flour and liquid that can be kneaded and shaped, pastry is made of flour, fat and a little water, and butter is a fat, so none of the options is exact.

**Intended answer: batter (not listed among the options).**



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Fish with little or no fats is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
White fish (cod, hake, whiting, plaice) store their fat in the liver and keep very little in the flesh, so they are low in fat. Herring is an oily fish (rich in fat), and crustaceans (crab, prawn) and molluscs (oyster, mussel) are shellfish, groups of animals and not a fat classification.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The carbohydrate found in the milk of mammals is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sugar of milk is lactose (milk sugar). Maltose is malt sugar, sucrose is cane or beet sugar, and galactose is only one of the two simple sugars (glucose and galactose) that make up lactose.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A deficiency of thiamin is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Thiamin is vitamin B1. Lack of it causes beriberi (weak muscles and damage to the nerves). Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C, rickets by lack of vitamin D and night blindness by lack of vitamin A.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: 1gm of carbohydrate will produce:
questions.corrige_markdown:
One gram of carbohydrate gives about 4 kcal (about 17 kJ). Protein gives the same, about 4 kcal per gram, and fat gives about 9 kcal per gram. So 9 kcal is the trap for fat, and 5 and 3 kcal are not energy values of any nutrient.

**Answer: C.**
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown:
Movement of body muscles is controlled by:

*Options as printed:* A) Electrical energy   B) Mechanical energy   C) Heat energy   D) Chemical energy
questions.corrige_markdown:
Muscles are made to contract by nerve impulses, which are electrical signals sent from the brain and nerves. The energy needed for the work comes from the chemical energy of food (ATP) and the result of the contraction is mechanical energy of movement. Because the word "controlled" can also be read as "powered by" (chemical energy), the printed question is open to discussion; the control signal is electrical.

**Intended answer: A (Electrical energy).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown: The chemical digestion of protein starts from:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Chemical digestion of protein begins in the stomach, where pepsin (with hydrochloric acid) breaks proteins into shorter chains called peptides. It is completed in the small intestine by trypsin and other enzymes. The mouth only starts the digestion of starch.

**Answer: B.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: The name given to tooth decay is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tooth decay is called dental caries: bacteria in plaque turn sugar into acid, which dissolves the enamel and makes holes (cavities). Plaque is the sticky film of bacteria, and periodontal disease and gingivitis are diseases of the gums.

**Answer: A.**
themes: dental health and diet in nutrition

questions.enonce_markdown: A vegan is also called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A vegan eats only plant foods and no animal product at all (no meat, fish, eggs, milk or honey), so a vegan is a strict vegetarian. An ovo vegetarian also eats eggs, a lacto vegetarian also eats milk products, and a lacto-ovo vegetarian eats both.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ---------------is a protein found in milk:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lactoglobulin (with lactalbumin and casein) is a protein of milk. Ovalbumin is the protein of egg white, mucin is the protein of saliva and mucus, and collagen is the protein of connective tissue in meat and bones.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is classified under flower vegetable?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Flower vegetables are those whose flower head is eaten: broccoli, cauliflower and artichoke. Chicory is a leaf vegetable and celery is a stalk vegetable, and parsley is a herb with leaves.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A breakfast meal should be prepared within--------- minutes:

*Options as printed:* A) 15   B) 45   C) 30   D) 25
questions.corrige_markdown:
The printed options (15, 45, 30 and 25 minutes) are not backed by a standard syllabus figure that can be proved: textbooks only say that breakfast should be quick and simple to prepare, because people are short of time in the morning. Planning ahead (laying the table and preparing foods the night before) keeps the time short. No single value can be marked with certainty, so this question is left open.

**Model answer: breakfast must be quick to prepare (usually quoted as about 15 to 30 minutes); the printed key cannot be established.**



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Water soluble vitamins are greatly affected by :
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin C and the B vitamins dissolve in water, so when vegetables are boiled in a lot of water for a long time these vitamins pass into the cooking water and are also destroyed by heat. That is why the cooking water should be used and vegetables should be cooked in little water for a short time. Steaming and frying lose less of them.

**Answer: A.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: A method of heat transfer by direct contact is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In conduction heat passes from particle to particle (or from one object to another) by direct contact, for example from a hot plate through a metal pot to the food. Convection is the movement of heated liquid or gas, and radiation (electromagnetic waves) travels without any contact.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is a stimulating beverage:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tea contains caffeine, which stimulates the nervous system; tea, coffee and cocoa are the stimulating beverages. Egg nog and milk are nourishing drinks, and fruit drinks are refreshing drinks rich in vitamin C. (The option names the tea leaves from which the drink is made.)

**Answer: A.**
themes: beverages and drinks in the diet

questions.enonce_markdown: Highly poisonous substances produced by moulds are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mycotoxins are poisons produced by moulds (for example aflatoxin on stored groundnuts and maize). The prefix "myco" means fungus. Spores are the reproductive cells of moulds, exotoxins are poisons released by bacteria, and bacteria are living organisms, not poisons.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Milk whose fats has been removed is called :
questions.corrige_markdown:
Skimmed milk is milk from which the cream (fat) has been removed. Condensed milk has had water removed, homogenized milk has had its fat globules broken up so that the cream does not rise, and pasteurized milk has been heated to kill harmful germs.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The normal dough consistency for a short crust pastry is ;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Shortcrust pastry is made by rubbing fat into flour and then adding just enough cold water to bind it into a stiff (firm) dough that can be rolled out. Too much water makes the dough soft and the pastry tough, an elastic dough is typical of bread dough (gluten developed by kneading), and a hard dough is too dry to roll.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Foods with high water content are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Foods with a high water content (fresh milk, meat, fish, vegetables, ripe fruits) spoil quickly because micro-organisms grow easily in moisture, so they are called perishable foods. "Diary" in the options is a misprint of dairy (milk products), and fruits are only one kind of food.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A method of cooking food with vapour rising from boiling water is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In steaming the food is cooked by the steam (vapour) that rises from boiling water, without touching the water. In boiling, simmering and poaching the food is in contact with the liquid itself.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most suitable breakfast is :

*Options as printed:* A) Dodo/Fried eggs with tea   B) Spaghetti/eggs with tea   C) Pawpaw slices,tea and bread slices   D) Corn pap/Accra with mangoe juice
questions.corrige_markdown:
A good breakfast should be light, quick to prepare and contain an energy food, a body-building food and a protective food (fruit). Option C (pawpaw, tea and bread) has fruit but little protein, option D (corn pap, accra and mango juice) has cereal, protein from beans and fruit juice but the accra is fried, and options A and B are heavy and lack fruit. More than one option can be defended, so the question is left open.

**Model answer: a light, balanced breakfast that includes a fruit, such as option C or option D; the printed key cannot be established.**



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A good conductor of heat is :
questions.corrige_markdown:
Metals are good conductors of heat, and steel passes heat quickly from the cooker to the food. Glass, enamel (a glassy coating) and earthenware (baked clay) are poor conductors: they heat slowly but keep the heat for a long time.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a group of legume from the following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Legumes are plants whose seeds grow in pods: beans, groundnuts (peanuts) and soya beans all belong to this group. The other options each contain a food that is not a legume: onion (bulb), maize (cereal), cucumber (fruit vegetable), millet (cereal) and rice (cereal).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The nutrients that provide energy for the body use :
questions.corrige_markdown:
The energy-giving nutrients are carbohydrates (about 4 kcal per gram) and fats (about 9 kcal per gram); proteins can also give energy but mainly build the body. Vitamins and mineral salts give no energy: they only regulate body processes and protect the body.

**Answer: A.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food
energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown: Salivary amylase converts:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Salivary amylase is the enzyme in saliva that starts the digestion of starch in the mouth, changing it to the double sugar maltose. Proteins are broken down by pepsin and trypsin, and sucrose by sucrase. The option "Maltose to Maltose" is a misprint and changes nothing.

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is a spice:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Spices come from the root, bark, seed or fruit of plants, and ginger is the underground stem (rhizome) of the ginger plant. Thyme, parsley and bay leaf are herbs because the leaves are used.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The green/black ring formed on the yolk when boiled,results from the reaction between-------- ---- and --------- :
questions.corrige_markdown:
When an egg is boiled for too long or not cooled quickly, sulphur from the egg white (hydrogen sulphide) reacts with the iron of the yolk to form iron sulphide, which is the grey-green ring around the yolk. It is harmless; plunging the egg into cold water after cooking prevents it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The scientific name of vitamin D is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin D is cholecalciferol (vitamin D3, made in the skin in sunlight). Tocopherol is vitamin E, ascorbic acid is vitamin C and retinol is vitamin A.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of wheat that contributes in producing flour is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The endosperm is the starchy inner part of the wheat grain and it is ground to make white flour. The bran (outer layers, pericarp) and the germ (embryo, rich in oil and vitamins) are mostly removed in white flour.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the greatest factors influencing food habits is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Food habits are strongly influenced by customs, the traditions, culture and religion of a community (what is eaten, when and how). Fallacies (wrong food beliefs) also play a part but customs are the greater factor, and "facts" and "habits" do not explain how habits are formed.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The habit of buying things not planned for is described as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Impulsive buying is buying on the spur of the moment, without a plan or a shopping list. Credit buying and hire purchase are ways of paying later, and wholesale means buying in large quantities for resale.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these are herbs?

*Options as printed:* A) Parsley and Nutmeg   B) Vanilla and Ginger   C) Tumeric and Parsley   D) Bayleaf and Garlic
questions.corrige_markdown:
Herbs are the leaves of plants used to flavour food (parsley, thyme, bay leaf, basil). Nutmeg, vanilla, ginger and turmeric are spices (seed, pod and underground stems). Each option contains something that is not a typical herb: nutmeg, vanilla, ginger and turmeric are spices, and garlic (a bulb) is usually put with the seasonings and is sometimes listed with the herbs. Option D is the closest to two herbs, but the printed question has no clean key.

**Intended answer: D (Bayleaf and Garlic).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The chemical reactions that take place in the body are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Metabolism is the name for all the chemical reactions that take place in the body. Catabolism (breaking down substances to release energy) and anabolism (building up substances) are the two parts of metabolism, and digestion is only the breakdown of food in the gut.

**Answer: B.**
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following are needed in the body in relatively large amounts:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats and proteins) are the nutrients needed in relatively large amounts, while micronutrients (vitamins and mineral elements) are needed only in small amounts. Minerals are micronutrients. Water is needed in large amounts but is not usually counted among the macronutrients in this question.

**Answer: B.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: _____ and _____ pairs of kitchen equipment facilitates cooking when placed together:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a well planned kitchen the sink (preparation and washing centre) and the cooker (cooking centre) are placed near each other with a work surface between them, so that vegetables are washed, prepared and cooked with the least walking. The refrigerator and freezer give off heat and should be kept away from the cooker.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ascorbic acid is also called?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, which prevents scurvy. Vitamin D is cholecalciferol, vitamin E is tocopherol, and vitamin B is a group of vitamins.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: A guest is a person who:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A guest is a person who is invited to a meal or an occasion and comes to share in it. The person who receives and entertains the guests is the host or hostess, and the person who serves food is the server or waiter.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The human body is composed of individual units called?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cell is the basic unit of the body. Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems; molecules are smaller than cells.

**Answer: A.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: First reaction of sugar on wet heat is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When sugar is heated with water (wet heat) it first dissolves in the water; on further boiling the solution becomes a syrup. Caramelization occurs with dry heat, when sugar is heated alone and turns brown.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following services is common in wedding:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At a wedding there are many guests, so a buffet service (the guests help themselves from a table where the dishes are displayed) is the one commonly used. It saves staff and serves many guests quickly. Plate service is used for small numbers.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most common fuel used in a traditional kitchen?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In traditional kitchens in Cameroon cooking is mostly done on an open fire or a three-stone hearth that burns firewood, which is cheap and easily found. Charcoal, kerosene and sawdust are used less.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The two proteins found in meat are :
questions.corrige_markdown:
The proteins of the connective tissue of meat are collagen (which turns to gelatine in moist cooking) and elastin (which does not soften). Caseinogen is the protein of milk, mucin is the protein of saliva, gelatine is a product of cooking collagen, and zein is the protein of maize.

**Answer: A.**
